subproblem.title: Uniform second-order expansion of det(I + tX + t²Y)
subproblem.statement:
Uniform second-order expansion of a determinant. For all N ∈ ℕ and κ ∈ ℝ there is C ∈ ℝ such that for every n ≤ N, all real n×n matrices X and Y with |X_ij| ≤ κ and |Y_ij| ≤ κ for all i, j, and every t ∈ ℝ with |t| ≤ 1:
 |det(I + tX + t²Y) − (1 + t·tr X + t²(tr Y + ((tr X)² − tr(X·X))/2))| ≤ C|t|³.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (κ : ℝ), ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ N → ∀ X Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, (∀ i j, |X i j| ≤ κ) → (∀ i j, |Y i j| ≤ κ) → ∀ t : ℝ, |t| ≤ 1 → |(1 + t • X + t ^ 2 • Y).det - (1 + t * X.trace + t ^ 2 * (Y.trace + (X.trace ^ 2 - (X * X).trace) / 2))| ≤ C * |t| ^ 3
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. The expansion det(I + E) = 1 + tr E + ½((tr E)² − tr(E²)) + O(|E|³) used in parent step (1c) for the Gram matrix b(t) = I + tc + t²d, made uniform in the entries. No dependencies.

Notation. For an n×n real matrix A let p_A := det(1 + 𝐗·A) ∈ ℝ[𝐗] (the entries of A are viewed as constant polynomials) and let e_k(A) be the coefficient of 𝐗^k in p_A. By Matrix.coeff_det_one_add_X_smul_eq_sum_minors, e_k(A) is the sum of the determinants of the k×k principal submatrices of A.

1. (Low coefficients and degree.) e_0(A) = 1 (the only 0-element subset gives the empty determinant 1), e_1(A) = tr A (Matrix.coeff_det_one_add_X_smul_one), and e_k(A) = 0 for k > n (there is no k-element subset of an n-element set), so deg p_A ≤ n.

2. (Second coefficient: e_2(A) = ((tr A)² − tr(A·A))/2.) Since 𝐗·A commutes with itself, (1 + 𝐗A)(1 − 𝐗A) = 1 − 𝐗²(A·A), hence p_A·p_{−A} = det(1 − 𝐗²(A·A)) (Matrix.det_mul). Compare the coefficients of 𝐗²:
 left side: e_0(A)e_2(−A) + e_1(A)e_1(−A) + e_2(A)e_0(−A) = 2e_2(A) − (tr A)², because e_1(−A) = −tr A and e_2(−A) = e_2(A) (every 2×2 principal submatrix N of −A is −N' for the corresponding submatrix N' of A, and det(−N') = (−1)² det N');
 right side: put B := A·A and q := p_B. Applying the ring homomorphism 'substitute −𝐗² for 𝐗' entrywise (RingHom.map_det) shows det(1 − 𝐗²B) = q(−𝐗²). Writing q = 1 + (tr B)𝐗 + 𝐗²r (Matrix.det_one_add_X_smul), q(−𝐗²) = 1 − (tr B)𝐗² + 𝐗⁴·r(−𝐗²), whose 𝐗²-coefficient is −tr B.
 Hence 2e_2(A) − (tr A)² = −tr(A·A).

3. (Crude bound for determinants.) If N is a k×k real matrix with |N_ij| ≤ b, then |det N| ≤ k!·b^k: the Leibniz formula writes det N as a sum of k! terms ±∏_i N_{σ(i)i}, each of absolute value ≤ b^k.

4. (Constants.) Put κ' := max(κ, 0), b := max(1, 2κ'), β := 2^N·N!·b^N and C := 3N²κ'² + N·β (≥ 0).

5. (Coefficient bound.) Let n ≤ N and let A be an n×n matrix with |A_ij| ≤ b. A k×k principal submatrix (k ≤ n; reindex its index set to Fin k by an equivalence, which does not change the determinant) has determinant of absolute value ≤ k!·b^k ≤ n!·b^n (b ≥ 1), and there are binom(n,k) ≤ 2^n ≤ 2^N of them. Hence |e_k(A)| ≤ 2^N·N!·b^N = β for every k.

6. (Expansion.) Fix n ≤ N, X, Y with entries bounded by κ (hence by κ'), and |t| ≤ 1. Put A := X + tY. Then I + tX + t²Y = I + tA and |A_ij| ≤ κ' + |t|κ' ≤ 2κ' ≤ b. Evaluating p_A at t (RingHom.map_det with the evaluation homomorphism) and using deg p_A < n + 3:
 det(I + tX + t²Y) = Σ_{k<n+3} e_k(A)t^k = 1 + t·tr A + t²e_2(A) + Σ_{i<n} e_{i+3}(A)t^{i+3}.
 By step 5 and |t|^{i+3} ≤ |t|³, the last sum has absolute value ≤ n·β|t|³ ≤ N·β|t|³.

7. (Comparison of the low-order terms.) tr A = tr X + t·tr Y and tr(A·A) = tr(X·X) + t(tr(X·Y) + tr(Y·X)) + t²tr(Y·Y). Using step 2,
 1 + t·tr A + t²e_2(A) − [1 + t·tr X + t²(tr Y + ((tr X)² − tr(X·X))/2)] = t³·[(2·tr X·tr Y − tr(X·Y) − tr(Y·X))/2 + t((tr Y)² − tr(Y·Y))/2].
 Each trace of a single matrix is a sum of n entries, so |tr X|, |tr Y| ≤ nκ'; each trace of a product is a sum of n² products of entries, so |tr(X·Y)|, |tr(Y·X)|, |tr(Y·Y)| ≤ n²κ'². With |t| ≤ 1 and n ≤ N the bracket has absolute value ≤ 2N²κ'² + N²κ'² = 3N²κ'².

8. (Conclusion.) Combining steps 6 and 7: |det(I + tX + t²Y) − (1 + t·tr X + t²(tr Y + ((tr X)² − tr(X·X))/2))| ≤ N·β|t|³ + 3N²κ'²|t|³ = C|t|³. ∎
proof_key_steps: det(I + tX + t²Y) = p_A(t) with A = X + tY and p_A = det(1 + 𝐗A), whose 𝐗^k-coefficient e_k(A) is the sum of the k×k principal minors.
e_0 = 1, e_1 = tr A, and e_2 = ((tr A)² − tr(A²))/2 from comparing 𝐗²-coefficients in det(1 + 𝐗A)·det(1 − 𝐗A) = det(1 − 𝐗²A²).
Leibniz bound |e_k(A)| ≤ 2^N·N!·b^N controls the cubic remainder; expanding tr A, tr(A²) in t costs at most 3N²κ'²|t|³.

subproblem.title: L² convergence of tangential gradients implies convergence of the Dirichlet energies
subproblem.statement: Convergence of L² energies. Data: P ∈ ℕ; a measure μ on ℝ^P; functions F_{k,j}, G_j : ℝ^P → ℝ for k ∈ ℕ and j ∈ Fin P. Hypotheses: every F_{k,j} and every G_j is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ; for every k, Σ_j F_{k,j}² is μ-integrable; ∫⁻ ofReal(Σ_j (F_{k,j} − G_j)²) dμ → 0 as k → ∞. Conclusion: Σ_j G_j² is μ-integrable, and ∫ Σ_j F_{k,j}² dμ → ∫ Σ_j G_j² dμ as k → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (F : ℕ → Fin P → Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Fin P → Euclid P → ℝ), (∀ k j, AEStronglyMeasurable (F k j) μ) → (∀ j, AEStronglyMeasurable (G j) μ) → (∀ k, Integrable (fun x => ∑ j : Fin P, (F k j x) ^ 2) μ) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (∑ j : Fin P, (F k j x - G j x) ^ 2) ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) → Integrable (fun x => ∑ j : Fin P, (G j x) ^ 2) μ ∧ Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, ∑ j : Fin P, (F k j x) ^ 2 ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, ∑ j : Fin P, (G j x) ^ 2 ∂μ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. The right-hand side of parent proof step 2 ('Dζ_k → d^Mζ in L²(H^m⌞M) for the seminorms |·|_{T_x} … Minkowski's inequality gives ∫_M|Dζ_k|²_{T_x} → ∫_M|∇^Mζ|²'), stated for a general measure. No dependencies.

Notation. a_k := Σ_jF_{k,j}², b := Σ_jG_j², d_k := Σ_j(F_{k,j} − G_j)². These are ≥ 0 and a.e.-strongly measurable (finite sums of products of a.e.-strongly measurable functions). Let δ_k := ∫⁻ ofReal(d_k) dμ, so δ_k → 0.

1. (Scalar inequalities.) For real x, y and ε > 0: x² ≤ (1 + ε)y² + (1 + 1/ε)(x − y)², since x² = y² + 2y(x − y) + (x − y)² and 2y(x − y) ≤ εy² + (x − y)²/ε (expand (εy − (x − y))² ≥ 0 and divide by ε). Summing over j: pointwise a_k ≤ (1 + ε)b + (1 + 1/ε)d_k and b ≤ (1 + ε)a_k + (1 + 1/ε)d_k. Also G_j² ≤ 2F_{k,j}² + 2(F_{k,j} − G_j)², so b ≤ 2a_k + 2d_k.

2. (Integrability.) Since δ_k → 0, δ_k < ∞ for all large k, and for such k the function d_k is integrable (a.e.-measurable with finite lintegral; hasFiniteIntegral_iff_ofReal). Fix one such k₀. Then 0 ≤ b ≤ 2a_{k₀} + 2d_{k₀}, an integrable function, and b is a.e.-strongly measurable, so b is integrable (Integrable.mono'). This is the first conclusion.

3. (∫d_k → 0.) For each k, ∫d_k dμ = (δ_k).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae), and toReal is continuous at 0, so ∫d_k dμ → 0.

4. (Convergence of the energies.) Let η > 0 and B := ∫b dμ ≥ 0. Put ε := min(1, η/(8(B + 1))), so 2εB ≤ η/4, and choose K such that for k ≥ K: δ_k < ∞ and 2(1 + 1/ε)∫d_k < η/4 (step 3). For k ≥ K, integrating the inequalities of step 1 (all functions involved are integrable) gives
 ∫a_k ≤ (1 + ε)B + (1 + 1/ε)∫d_k and B ≤ (1 + ε)∫a_k + (1 + 1/ε)∫d_k.
 From the first, ∫a_k − B ≤ εB + (1 + 1/ε)∫d_k < η. Inserting the first into the second and using ε ≤ 1 (so ε(1 + 1/ε) = ε + 1 ≤ 2 ≤ 1 + 1/ε),
 B − ∫a_k ≤ ε∫a_k + (1 + 1/ε)∫d_k ≤ ε(1 + ε)B + (ε(1 + 1/ε) + (1 + 1/ε))∫d_k ≤ 2εB + 2(1 + 1/ε)∫d_k < η.
 Hence |∫a_k − ∫b| < η for all k ≥ K, i.e. ∫Σ_jF_{k,j}² dμ → ∫Σ_jG_j² dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pointwise: (x)² ≤ (1+ε)y² + (1+1/ε)(x−y)², summed over j, compares the energies a_k, b with the error d_k in both directions.
Finite ∫⁻ d_k for large k and b ≤ 2a_k + 2d_k give integrability of b; ∫d_k → 0.
Choosing ε small and then k large gives |∫a_k − ∫b| < η.

subproblem.statement: Small perturbations of the identity. Data: P ∈ ℕ; Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P; Λ, t ∈ ℝ. Hypotheses: Z is C¹; ‖DZ(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ ℝ^P; |t|Λ < 1. Conclusion: the map Φ(x) := x + tZ(x) is injective; DΦ(x) = I + tDZ(x) for every x; and DΦ(x) is injective for every x. (D = fderiv ℝ.)

Source. Parent proof step (1c): 'For |t| < 1/(1 + Λ), Φ_t is C^∞ and injective with injective derivative I + tDZ (the mean value inequality gives |Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| ≥ (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b|)'. No dependencies.

1. (Derivative.) Z is differentiable everywhere (C¹). The identity has derivative I and x ↦ tZ(x) has derivative tDZ(x), so Φ has derivative I + tDZ(x) at every x (sum and constant-multiple rules: (hasFDerivAt_id x).add ((DZ).const_smul t)). This is the second conjunct.

2. (Lipschitz bound.) By the mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le) and ‖DZ‖ ≤ Λ, |Z(b) − Z(a)| ≤ Λ|b − a| for all a, b ∈ ℝ^P.

3. (Φ is injective.) If Φ(a) = Φ(b), then a − b = t(Z(b) − Z(a)), so |a − b| = |t||Z(b) − Z(a)| ≤ |t|Λ|a − b|. If a ≠ b, dividing by |a − b| > 0 gives 1 ≤ |t|Λ, contradicting |t|Λ < 1. Hence a = b.

4. (DΦ(x) is injective.) DΦ(x) is linear, so it suffices to show its kernel is trivial. If (I + tDZ(x))u = 0 then u = −tDZ(x)u, and |u| = |t||DZ(x)u| ≤ |t|‖DZ(x)‖|u| ≤ |t|Λ|u|. If u ≠ 0 this gives 1 ≤ |t|Λ, a contradiction; so u = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: DΦ(x) = I + tDZ(x) by the sum and constant-multiple rules.
Mean value inequality: |Z(b) − Z(a)| ≤ Λ|b − a|, so Φ(a) = Φ(b) forces |a − b| ≤ |t|Λ|a − b| and a = b.
(I + tDZ(x))u = 0 forces |u| ≤ |t|Λ|u|, so u = 0.

subproblem.title: Admissible ambient extension Z of the normal variation ζν, with its tangential derivative
subproblem.statement: Admissible ambient extension of a normal variation. Data: P ∈ ℕ; U, O, M, C ⊆ ℝ^P; ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P; ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ. Hypotheses: U and O are open; M ⊆ U and M ⊆ O; ν is C^∞ on O; |ν(x)| = 1 for x ∈ M; ζ is C^∞ on ℝ^P; C is compact, C ⊆ M, and ζ(x) = 0 for every x ∈ M ∖ C. Conclusion: there is a C^∞ map Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport Z ⊆ U such that (a) Z(x) = ζ(x)ν(x) for every x ∈ M; (b) DZ(x)τ = (Dζ(x)τ)ν(x) + ζ(x)Dν(x)τ for every x ∈ M and τ ∈ span(tangentSpace M x); (c) for every x ∈ M with x ∉ tsupport Z, ζ(x) = 0 and Dζ(x)τ = 0 for every τ ∈ span(tangentSpace M x). Here D = fderiv ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U O M C : Set (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P → Euclid P) (ζ : Euclid P → ℝ), IsOpen U → IsOpen O → M ⊆ U → M ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ν O → (∀ x ∈ M, ‖ν x‖ = 1) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ζ → IsCompact C → C ⊆ M → (∀ x ∈ M, x ∉ C → ζ x = 0) → ∃ Z : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) Z ∧ HasCompactSupport Z ∧ tsupport Z ⊆ U ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, Z x = ζ x • ν x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ τ ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x), fderiv ℝ Z x τ = fderiv ℝ ζ x τ • ν x + ζ x • fderiv ℝ ν x τ) ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, x ∉ tsupport Z → ζ x = 0 ∧ ∀ τ ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x), fderiv ℝ ζ x τ = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof steps (1a)–(1b) and the remark in (1c) that ζ̃ and Dζ̃ vanish on T_xM at points of M outside tsupport Z. Departure: the projection Π onto A₀ used in (1a) plays no role later and is omitted. No dependencies.

1. (Cut-off.) C is compact and C ⊆ M ⊆ O ∩ U, an open set. Since ℝ^P is locally compact, there is a compact L with C ⊆ interior(L) and L ⊆ O ∩ U (exists_compact_between). The smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (with smoothness ⊤), applied to the open set interior(L) and the closed set C ⊆ interior(L), gives β : ℝ^P → ℝ, C^∞, with support β = interior(L) and β(x) = 1 for x ∈ C. Then tsupport β = closure(interior L) ⊆ L because L is closed; so tsupport β is compact and tsupport β ⊆ O ∩ U.

2. (Definition and smoothness of Z.) Put Z(y) := (β(y)ζ(y))ν(y). Let y ∈ ℝ^P. If y ∈ O, then βζ is C^∞ at y and ν is C^∞ at y (ν is C^∞ on the open set O ∋ y), so Z is C^∞ at y. If y ∉ O, then y ∉ tsupport β (as tsupport β ⊆ O); the complement of tsupport β is an open neighbourhood of y on which β = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so Z = 0 near y and Z is C^∞ at y. Thus Z is C^∞ at every point, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ⊤ Z (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt).

3. (Support.) tsupport Z ⊆ tsupport(βζ) ⊆ tsupport β (tsupport_smul_subset_left, tsupport_mul_subset_left), so tsupport Z ⊆ U. Z vanishes outside the compact closed set tsupport β, hence Z has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro').

4. ((a) Z = ζν on M.) Let x ∈ M. If x ∈ C then β(x) = 1 and Z(x) = ζ(x)ν(x). If x ∉ C then ζ(x) = 0 by hypothesis, so Z(x) = 0 = ζ(x)ν(x).

5. ((b) The tangential derivative.) Let x ∈ M and v ∈ tangentSpace M x, witnessed by γ: C¹ on (−1,1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = x, γ'(0) = v. Z and ζ are differentiable everywhere, and ν is differentiable at x (x ∈ O, O open). By the chain rule s ↦ Z(γ(s)) has derivative DZ(x)v at 0; by the chain and product rules (HasDerivAt.smul) s ↦ ζ(γ(s))ν(γ(s)) has derivative ζ(x)Dν(x)v + (Dζ(x)v)ν(x) at 0. By step 4 these two functions coincide on (−1,1), a neighbourhood of 0, so their derivatives coincide: DZ(x)v = (Dζ(x)v)ν(x) + ζ(x)Dν(x)v. Both sides are linear in v (DZ(x), Dζ(x), Dν(x) are linear maps), so by induction over the span (zero, sums, scalar multiples; Submodule.span_induction) the identity holds for every τ ∈ span(tangentSpace M x).

6. ((c) Vanishing off tsupport Z.) Let x ∈ M with x ∉ tsupport Z. The complement N of tsupport Z is an open neighbourhood of x on which Z = 0. For y ∈ N ∩ M, ζ(y)ν(y) = Z(y) = 0 by (a) and ν(y) ≠ 0 since |ν(y)| = 1, hence ζ(y) = 0; in particular ζ(x) = 0. Now let v ∈ tangentSpace M x with curve γ as in step 5. γ is continuous at 0 with γ(0) = x, so γ(s) ∈ N for all small |s|, and γ(s) ∈ M for |s| < 1; hence ζ∘γ vanishes on a neighbourhood of 0 and its derivative at 0 is 0. By the chain rule this derivative equals Dζ(x)v, so Dζ(x)v = 0. By linearity Dζ(x)τ = 0 for every τ ∈ span(tangentSpace M x). ∎

Z := βζν is C^∞ (near points of O a product of smooth maps, elsewhere locally 0), compactly supported in U, and equals ζν on M.
Differentiating along C¹ curves in M gives DZ(x)τ = (Dζ(x)τ)ν(x) + ζ(x)Dν(x)τ, and off tsupport Z gives ζ(x) = 0 and Dζ(x)τ = 0; extend to span T_xM by linearity.

subproblem.title: Second-order upper bound for the tangential Jacobian of I + tL when trace(P_S L) = 0
subproblem.statement:
Second-order bound for the area Jacobian. For all P ∈ ℕ and Λ ∈ ℝ there is C ∈ ℝ such that for every linear subspace S ⊆ ℝ^P, every linear map L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with operator norm ‖L‖ ≤ Λ and trace(P_S∘L) = 0, and every t ∈ ℝ with |t| ≤ 1:
 √det(((I + tL)∘ι_S)*((I + tL)∘ι_S)) ≤ 1 + (t²/2)·Σ_{j=1}^P (|L(P_Se_j) − P_S L(P_Se_j)|² − P_Se_j·L(P_S L(P_Se_j))) + C|t|³,
where P_S is the orthogonal projection onto S, ι_S : S → ℝ^P the inclusion, * the adjoint for the inner products of S and ℝ^P, det the determinant of an endomorphism of S, and e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. The Taylor expansion of J_t = √det(b(t)) in parent step (1c) (Simon Ch. 2, 5.2–5.4), for a linear map whose first-order term vanishes. Departure: instead of expanding √(1 + u) we use √y ≤ (1 + y)/2 for y ≥ 0, which is exact to second order because the first-order coefficient vanishes; no differentiation in t is needed. Dependency: det_second_order (Lean name Submission.codim1_hcp_stab_det_second_order).

Notation. ι := ι_S, T := (I + tL)∘ι : S → ℝ^P, G := T*T : S → S, u_j := P_Se_j, and Q := Σ_j (|Lu_j − P_S Lu_j|² − u_j·L(P_S Lu_j)).

1. (Constant.) Let C₁ be the constant of det_second_order for N := P and κ := 2|Λ| + Λ², and put C := max(C₁, 0)/2. Fix S, L, t as in the statement; note Λ ≥ ‖L‖ ≥ 0.

2. (Orthonormal basis; expansion of P_S.) Let n := dim S; then n ≤ P (Submodule.finrank_le). Let τ_1, …, τ_n be an orthonormal basis of S (stdOrthonormalBasis, reindexed by Fin n). For every w ∈ ℝ^P, P_S w = Σ_k (τ_k·w)τ_k: apply OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr' to the orthogonal projection π(w) ∈ S of w and use τ_k·π(w) = τ_k·w (Submodule.inner_orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_of_mem_left).

3. (One trace, two bases.) For every linear R : ℝ^P → ℝ^P:
 (i) trace(P_S∘R) = Σ_j u_j·R u_j. Indeed P_S∘R = P_S∘(P_S∘R) (P_S² = P_S), so trace(P_S∘R) = trace((P_S∘R)∘P_S) (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'), and computing this trace in the standard orthonormal basis (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with EuclideanSpace.basisFun) gives Σ_j e_j·P_S R P_S e_j = Σ_j P_Se_j·R P_Se_j (P_S self-adjoint).
 (ii) trace(P_S∘R) = Σ_i τ_i·Rτ_i. Indeed trace(P_S∘R) = trace(R∘P_S) and P_S = ι∘π, so (trace_comp_comm' twice) trace(P_S∘R) = trace_S(π∘R∘ι); computing the latter in the basis τ (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner) gives Σ_i τ_i·π(Rτ_i) = Σ_i τ_i·Rτ_i.
 Consequently Σ_j u_j·R u_j = Σ_i τ_i·Rτ_i.   (★)

4. (Matrix of G.) H^m⌞M, and (ii) for every ζ locally Lipschitz on M vanishing on M outside a compact C ⊆ M there are a compact C' ⊆ M and C^∞ compactly supported ζ_k vanishing on M ∖ C' with ζ_k → ζ uniformly on M and ∫⁻_M ofReal(Σ_j(Dζ_k(x)(P_xe_j) − d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))²) dH^m → 0; (hSmooth) ∫_M w·ζ̃² dH^m ≤ ∫_M Σ_j(Dζ̃(x)(P_xe_j))² dH^m for every C^∞ compactly supported ζ̃ that vanishes on M outside some compact subset of M. Conclusion: for every ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ locally Lipschitz on M that vanishes on M outside some compact C ⊆ M, ∫_M w·ζ² dH^m ≤ ∫_M Σ_j(d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))² dH^m. Here d^M_xζ = fderivWithin ℝ ζ M x, D = fderiv ℝ, e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1, H^m = μHE[m], Bochner integrals over M.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 2 (extension to locally Lipschitz ζ). Departure: the integrability of |∇^Mζ|² is obtained from the L² convergence (energy_convergence) rather than from a Lipschitz bound along curves; the sibling lipschitz_approx enters as hypothesis (hApprox) and the sibling locally_closed as the hypothesis that M is measurable. Dependency: energy_convergence (Lean name Submission.codim1_hcp_stab_energy_convergence).

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; P_x := orthogonal projection (Submodule.starProjection) onto span(tangentSpace M x); e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1; d^M_xζ := fderivWithin ℝ ζ M x; D := fderiv ℝ. Hypotheses of the lean_statement, in order: (Meas) M is measurable; (hfin) H^m(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ M; (hw) w is continuous on M; (hP) x ↦ P_xu is continuous on M for every u; (hApprox) = (i) ∧ (ii): (i) for ζ locally Lipschitz on M and every j, x ↦ d^M_xζ(P_xe_j) is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^m⌞M; (ii) for ζ locally Lipschitz on M vanishing on M off a compact C ⊆ M there are a compact C' ⊆ M and ζ_k (C^∞, compact support) with ζ_k = 0 on M ∖ C', ζ_k → ζ uniformly on M and ∫⁻_M ofReal(Σ_j(Dζ_k(x)(P_xe_j) − d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))²) dH^m → 0; (hSmooth) ∫_M w·ζ̃² dH^m ≤ ∫_M Σ_j(Dζ̃(x)(P_xe_j))² dH^m for every C^∞ compactly supported ζ̃ vanishing on M off some compact subset of M. Then ζ is locally Lipschitz on M and vanishes on M off a compact C ⊆ M.

1. (Approximants.) Let ζ and C be as in the conclusion. By (hApprox)(ii) there are a compact C' ⊆ M and C^∞ compactly supported ζ_k with ζ_k = 0 on M ∖ C', ζ_k → ζ uniformly on M, and ∫⁻_M ofReal(Σ_j(Dζ_k(x)(P_xe_j) − d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))²) dH^m → 0.

2. (Tangential derivatives of ζ_k vanish off C'.) Let x ∈ M ∖ C' and v ∈ tangentSpace M x with curve γ (C¹ on (−1,1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = x, γ'(0) = v). C' is closed and γ is continuous at 0, so γ(s) ∉ C' for all small |s|; also γ(s) ∈ M for |s| < 1. Hence ζ_k∘γ = 0 near 0, and by the chain rule Dζ_k(x)v = (ζ_k∘γ)'(0) = 0. By linearity Dζ_k(x)τ = 0 for every τ ∈ span(tangentSpace M x); in particular Dζ_k(x)(P_xe_j) = 0.

3. (Right-hand side.) Put F_{k,j}(x) := Dζ_k(x)(P_xe_j) and G_j(x) := d^M_xζ(P_xe_j). F_{k,j} is continuous on M (Dζ_k is continuous and x ↦ P_xe_j is continuous on M by (hP)), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for H^m⌞M (M measurable by (Meas)). Σ_jF_{k,j}² ≤ P·sup|Dζ_k|² (|P_xe_j| ≤ 1; Dζ_k is bounded since ζ_k is C^∞ with compact support) and vanishes on M ∖ C' by step 2; as H^m(C') < ∞ by (hfin), Σ_jF_{k,j}² is integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero). G_j is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^m⌞M by (hApprox)(i). Applying energy_convergence with μ := H^m⌞M and step 1:
 ∫_M Σ_jF_{k,j}² dH^m → ∫_M Σ_jG_j² dH^m.

4. (Left-hand side.) K₀ := C ∪ C' is a compact subset of M, so H^m(K₀) < ∞ by (hfin), and there are B_w, B_z with |w| ≤ B_w and |ζ| ≤ B_z on K₀ (w is continuous on M by (hw), and ζ is continuous on M because it is locally Lipschitz on M). By uniform convergence, for all large k we have |ζ_k − ζ| < 1 on M, hence |ζ_k| ≤ B_z + 1 on K₀; and on M ∖ K₀, ζ_k = 0. So for all large k, |w·ζ_k²| ≤ B_w(B_z + 1)²·1_{K₀} on M, an H^m⌞M-integrable function. Each w·ζ_k² is continuous on M, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for H^m⌞M, and w·ζ_k² → w·ζ² pointwise on M. By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), ∫_M w·ζ_k² dH^m → ∫_M w·ζ² dH^m.

5. (Passage to the limit.) For every k, ζ_k is C^∞ with compact support and vanishes on M ∖ C', C' ⊆ M compact, so (hSmooth) gives ∫_M w·ζ_k² ≤ ∫_M Σ_jF_{k,j}². Letting k → ∞ with steps 3 and 4 (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto') yields ∫_M w·ζ² dH^m ≤ ∫_M Σ_j(d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))² dH^m. ∎

Tangential derivatives of ζ_k vanish off C', so the smooth energies are integrable; energy_convergence (with (hApprox)(i) for measurability) gives convergence of the right-hand sides.
Dominated convergence on the compact C ∪ C' gives convergence of ∫_M wζ_k²; (hSmooth) for each ζ_k and passage to the limit give the inequality.

subproblem.statement: Tangent projection of a hypersurface in A₀. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P; ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Hypotheses: dim A₀ = m + 1; M ⊆ A₀; M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M); for every x ∈ M, ν(x) ∈ A₀, |ν(x)| = 1 and ν(x)·v = 0 for every v ∈ tangentSpace M x. Conclusion: (i) for every x ∈ M and u ∈ ℝ^P, P_x u = Π u − (ν(x)·u)ν(x), where P_x is the orthogonal projection onto span(tangentSpace M x) and Π the orthogonal projection onto A₀ (both Submodule.starProjection); (ii) if moreover ν is continuous on M, then x ↦ P_x u is continuous on M for every u ∈ ℝ^P.

Source. Parent proof items (0.1) (T_x ⊆ A₀, A₀ = T_x ⊕ ℝν(x)) and (0.5) (continuity of x ↦ P_x on M). Departure: continuity is obtained from the hypersurface identity P_x = Π − ν(x)⊗ν(x) instead of the chart formula P_{ψ(v)} = Dψ(Dψ*Dψ)^{-1}Dψ*. Dependency: chart_tangent_space (Lean name Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv).

Notation. For x ∈ M: T_x := tangentSpace M x, S_x := span_ℝ T_x, P_x := orthogonal projection onto S_x, Π := orthogonal projection onto A₀.

1. (T_x ⊆ A₀.) Let x ∈ M and v ∈ T_x, witnessed by γ : ℝ → ℝ^P that is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, has γ(0) = x and derivative v at 0. For 0 < |s| < 1 the slope s⁻¹(γ(0 + s) − γ(0)) lies in A₀, because γ(s) and γ(0) lie in M ⊆ A₀ and A₀ is a linear subspace. By HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero these slopes tend to v along the punctured neighbourhood filter of 0, and A₀ is closed (a finite-dimensional subspace, Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). Hence v ∈ A₀ (IsClosed.mem_of_tendsto).

2. (A chart and the dimension of S_x.) By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M at x there are open V ⊆ ℝ^m, W ⊆ ℝ^P and ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P with x ∈ W, ψ C¹ on V, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for z ∈ V. Since x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), x = ψ(v₀) for some v₀ ∈ V. By chart_tangent_space (with r = 1), T_x = range Dψ(v₀). This range is a linear subspace, so S_x = range Dψ(v₀) (Submodule.span_eq), and since Dψ(v₀) : ℝ^m → ℝ^P is injective, dim S_x = m (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).

3. (S_x = (ℝν(x))^⊥ ∩ A₀.) Write n := ν(x) and H := (ℝn)^⊥ ⊓ A₀. Since n ∈ A₀ and n ≠ 0 (|n| = 1), the line ℝn has dimension 1 and is contained in A₀, so Submodule.finrank_add_inf_finrank_orthogonal gives 1 + dim H = dim A₀ = m + 1, i.e. dim H = m. Every v ∈ T_x satisfies n·v = 0 (hypothesis) and v ∈ A₀ (step 1), so T_x ⊆ H and therefore S_x ≤ H (Submodule.span_le). Both have dimension m, so S_x = H (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).

4. (The projection formula.) Fix u ∈ ℝ^P and put p := Πu − (n·u)n. Then p ∈ A₀ (Πu ∈ A₀ and n ∈ A₀), and
 n·p = n·Πu − (n·u)(n·n) = Πn·u − n·u = 0,
because Π is self-adjoint (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right), Πn = n (n ∈ A₀) and n·n = |n|² = 1. So p ∈ H = S_x. For every w ∈ H = S_x,
 (u − p)·w = (u − Πu)·w + (n·u)(n·w) = 0,
since w ∈ A₀ and u − Πu ∈ A₀^⊥ (Submodule.sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal), and n·w = 0 because w ∈ (ℝn)^⊥. A vector p ∈ S_x with u − p ⊥ S_x is the orthogonal projection of u onto S_x (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). Hence P_x u = Πu − (ν(x)·u)ν(x) for every x ∈ M and u ∈ ℝ^P, which is the first conjunct.

5. (Continuity.) Assume ν is continuous on M and fix u ∈ ℝ^P. The map x ↦ Πu − (ν(x)·u)ν(x) is continuous on M: it is a constant minus the product of the continuous scalar function x ↦ ν(x)·u (ContinuousOn.inner) and the continuous map ν. By step 4 it coincides on M with x ↦ P_x u, which is therefore continuous on M (ContinuousOn.congr). This is the second conjunct. ∎

p := Πu − (ν(x)·u)ν(x) lies in span T_xM and u − p ⊥ span T_xM, so P_x u = p; continuity of x ↦ P_x u on M follows from that of ν.

subproblem.statement: Shape operator of a hypersurface in A₀. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M, O ⊆ ℝ^P; ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Conclusion: for every x ∈ M and every τ ∈ S_x := span(tangentSpace M x), Dν(x)τ ∈ S_x, and η·Dν(x)τ = τ·Dν(x)η for every η ∈ S_x, where Dν(x) = fderiv ℝ ν x.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof items (0.2) (D_τν ∈ T_xM) and (0.3) (symmetry, Simon 4.26). Departure: the chart used for (0.3) is the C² chart supplied directly by IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 m M, so smooth_charts is not needed. Dependencies: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv), tangent_projection (Submission.codim1_hcp_stab_tangent_projection).

Notation. T_y := tangentSpace M y, S_y := span T_y, P_y := orthogonal projection onto S_y, Π := orthogonal projection onto A₀, Dν(y) := fderiv ℝ ν y.

0. (Preliminaries.) IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 m M implies IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M: every chart that is C² on V is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.of_le) and the other chart conditions do not change. For y ∈ O, ν is differentiable at y with derivative Dν(y), since O is open and ν is C¹ on O. Fix x ∈ M (so x ∈ O) and write n := ν(x).

1. (A C² chart at x.) IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 m M at x gives open V ⊆ ℝ^m, W ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W and ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, C² on V, injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for z ∈ V. As x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), x = ψ(v₀) with v₀ ∈ V. By chart_tangent_space (with r = 2), T_{ψ(v)} = range Dψ(v) for every v ∈ V. In particular T_x = range Dψ(v₀) is a linear subspace and S_x = range Dψ(v₀) = T_x.

2. (Dν(x) maps S_x into S_x.) Let τ ∈ S_x = T_x, witnessed by a curve γ that is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, has γ(0) = x and γ'(0) = τ. By the chain rule, s ↦ ν(γ(s)) has derivative Dν(x)τ at 0.
 (a) Let Π^⊥ be the orthogonal projection onto A₀^⊥, a continuous linear map. For s ∈ (−1,1), ν(γ(s)) ∈ A₀ = (A₀^⊥)^⊥, so Π^⊥(ν(γ(s))) = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff, Submodule.orthogonal_orthogonal). Thus Π^⊥∘ν∘γ vanishes on a neighbourhood of 0; its derivative at 0, which by the chain rule is Π^⊥(Dν(x)τ), is therefore 0 (uniqueness of derivatives). Hence Dν(x)τ ∈ (A₀^⊥)^⊥ = A₀.
 (b) For s ∈ (−1,1), ν(γ(s))·ν(γ(s)) = |ν(γ(s))|² = 1. Differentiating at 0 (HasDerivAt.inner) gives n·Dν(x)τ + Dν(x)τ·n = 0, i.e. n·Dν(x)τ = 0.
 (c) By tangent_projection (first conjunct; its hypotheses hold with IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M), P_x(Dν(x)τ) = Π(Dν(x)τ) − (n·Dν(x)τ)n = Dν(x)τ, using (a) (Πw = w for w ∈ A₀) and (b). As P_x takes values in S_x, Dν(x)τ ∈ S_x.

3. (A function vanishing on V.) Fix a ∈ ℝ^m and define f_a(v) := ν(ψ(v))·(Dψ(v)a). For v ∈ V we have ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ M and Dψ(v)a ∈ range Dψ(v) = T_{ψ(v)} (step 1), so f_a(v) = 0 by the normality hypothesis at ψ(v). Since V is an open neighbourhood of v₀, f_a vanishes near v₀ and its derivative at v₀ is 0.

4. (Its derivative.) ψ is differentiable at v₀ and ν at ψ(v₀) = x, so v ↦ ν(ψ(v)) has derivative Dν(x)∘Dψ(v₀) at v₀ (chain rule). Since ψ is C² on the open set V, v ↦ Dψ(v) is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen), so it has derivative D²ψ(v₀) := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) v₀ at v₀, and v ↦ Dψ(v)a has derivative b ↦ D²ψ(v₀)(b)(a) (HasFDerivAt.clm_apply). By the product rule for the inner product (HasFDerivAt.inner, fderivInnerCLM_apply) and step 3, for all b ∈ ℝ^m:
 (★) n·(D²ψ(v₀)(b)(a)) + (Dν(x)Dψ(v₀)b)·(Dψ(v₀)a) = 0.

5. (Schwarz.) ψ is C² on a neighbourhood of v₀, so its second derivative at v₀ is symmetric: D²ψ(v₀)(a)(b) = D²ψ(v₀)(b)(a) for all a, b (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt; over ℝ, minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2).

6. (Symmetry.) Let τ, η ∈ S_x = range Dψ(v₀), say τ = Dψ(v₀)a and η = Dψ(v₀)b. Applying (★) to the pairs (a, b) and (b, a) and using step 5,
 (Dν(x)Dψ(v₀)b)·(Dψ(v₀)a) = −n·D²ψ(v₀)(b)(a) = −n·D²ψ(v₀)(a)(b) = (Dν(x)Dψ(v₀)a)·(Dψ(v₀)b).
 Hence η·Dν(x)τ = (Dν(x)τ)·η = (Dν(x)η)·τ = τ·Dν(x)η. Together with step 2 this proves the claim for every x ∈ M. ∎

In a C² chart ψ with x = ψ(v₀), chart_tangent_space gives f_a(v) := ν(ψ(v))·Dψ(v)a ≡ 0 on V; differentiating at v₀: (Dν(x)Dψ(v₀)b)·Dψ(v₀)a = −ν(x)·D²ψ(v₀)(b)(a).
Symmetry of D²ψ(v₀) (Schwarz) makes (a,b) ↦ (Dν(x)Dψ(v₀)a)·Dψ(v₀)b symmetric, i.e. η·Dν(x)τ = τ·Dν(x)η on span T_xM = range Dψ(v₀).

subproblem.title: Stability inequality B.1 for smooth compactly supported test functions (second variation)
subproblem.statement:
Stability inequality B.1 for smooth test functions. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; U ⊆ ℝ^P; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P; ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Hypotheses: those of the parent theorem — U open, M ⊆ U, dim A₀ = m + 1, M ⊆ A₀, M an embedded C^r m-dimensional submanifold for every r ∈ ℕ, H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ν C^∞ on some open O ⊇ M, and for x ∈ M: ν(x) ∈ A₀, |ν(x)| = 1, ν(x)·v = 0 for v ∈ tangentSpace M x, trace(P_x∘Dν(x)) = 0; and for every C^∞ compactly supported Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with tsupport Z ⊆ U there is t₀ > 0 with H^m(M ∩ tsupport Z) ≤ H^m({x + tZ(x) : x ∈ M ∩ tsupport Z}) for |t| < t₀ — together with: (Meas) M is measurable; (hArea) for every measurable E ⊆ M and every C¹ map Φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P that is injective on E with DΦ(x) injective for x ∈ E, H^m(Φ(E)) ≤ ∫⁻_E ofReal(√det((DΦ(x)ι_x)*(DΦ(x)ι_x))) dH^m(x), where ι_x is the inclusion of span(tangentSpace M x). Conclusion: for every C^∞ ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support that vanishes on M outside some compact C ⊆ M,
 ∫_M (Σ_j |Dν(x)(P_xe_j)|²)·ζ(x)² dH^m(x) ≤ ∫_M Σ_j (Dζ(x)(P_xe_j))² dH^m(x),
with P_x the orthogonal projection onto span(tangentSpace M x), e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1, D = fderiv ℝ, H^m = μHE[m], Bochner integrals over M.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 1 ((1a)–(1d)): B.1 for smooth ζ̃ by the second variation. Departures: (i) the two differentiations under the integral sign in (1c) are replaced by integrating the uniform pointwise second-order upper bound for the Jacobian (jacobian_bound) and applying second_variation_nonneg; (ii) continuity of x ↦ P_x on M comes from tangent_projection; (iii) the sibling area_formula enters as hypothesis (hArea) (only its '≤' half is needed) and the sibling locally_closed as hypothesis (Meas). Dependencies (Lean names Submission.codim1_hcp_stab_*): tangent_projection, shape_operator, variation_field, jacobian_bound, normal_variation_algebra, second_variation_nonneg, perturbation_injective.

Hypotheses of the lean_statement, in order, with the labels used below: (hU) U is open; (hMU) M ⊆ U; (hA₀) dim A₀ = m + 1; (hMA) M ⊆ A₀; (hM) IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r m M for every r ∈ ℕ; (Meas) M is measurable; (hfin, finiteness) H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; (hO) an open O ⊇ M on which ν is C^∞; (hν, normality) ν(x) ∈ A₀, |ν(x)| = 1 and ν(x)·v = 0 for v ∈ tangentSpace M x, for x ∈ M; (htr, trace hypothesis H ≡ 0) trace(P_x∘Dν(x)) = 0 for x ∈ M; (hdef, deformation/minimality hypothesis) every C^∞ compactly supported Z with tsupport Z ⊆ U has t₀ > 0 with H^m(M ∩ tsupport Z) ≤ H^m({x + tZ(x) : x ∈ M ∩ tsupport Z}) for |t| < t₀; (hArea) for measurable E ⊆ M and C¹ Φ injective on E with DΦ(x) injective on E, H^m(Φ(E)) ≤ ∫⁻_E ofReal(√det((DΦ(x)ι_x)*(DΦ(x)ι_x))) dH^m. Then ζ is C^∞ with compact support and vanishes on M off a compact C ⊆ M.

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; for x ∈ M: S_x := span(tangentSpace M x), P_x its orthogonal projection, ι_x : S_x → ℝ^P the inclusion; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1; a(x) := Σ_j|Dν(x)(P_xe_j)|², f₁(x) := Σ_j(Dζ(x)(P_xe_j))², q(x) := f₁(x) − ζ(x)²a(x). The claim is ∫_M a·ζ² ≤ ∫_M f₁.

1. (Variation field.) Let O be the open set of the hypothesis and C' ⊆ M compact with ζ = 0 on M ∖ C'. variation_field (applied to U, O, M, C', ν, ζ; |ν| = 1 on M) gives Z, C^∞ with compact support and tsupport Z ⊆ U, such that (b) DZ(x)τ = (Dζ(x)τ)ν(x) + ζ(x)Dν(x)τ for x ∈ M and τ ∈ S_x, and (c) ζ(x) = 0 and Dζ(x)τ = 0 (τ ∈ S_x) for x ∈ M ∖ tsupport Z.

2. (Constants.) DZ is continuous with compact support, so there is Λ (≥ 0) with ‖DZ(x)‖ ≤ Λ for all x. Let C₀ be the constant given by jacobian_bound for (P, Λ), and t₀ > 0 the time given by the deformation hypothesis (hdef) for Z (which is C^∞, compactly supported, tsupport Z ⊆ U).

3. (Geometry at points of M.) By tangent_projection (with IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M; ν is continuous on O ⊇ M), x ↦ P_xu is continuous on M for every u. By shape_operator (with IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 m M; ν is C¹ on O), for x ∈ M: Dν(x)τ ∈ S_x and η·Dν(x)τ = τ·Dν(x)η for τ, η ∈ S_x. Dν is continuous on the open set O (ν is C^∞ there).

4. (Pointwise Jacobian bound.) Fix x ∈ M and t with |t| ≤ 1. The normality hypothesis (hν) ν(x)·v = 0 for v ∈ tangentSpace M x extends by linearity to v ∈ S_x, and |ν(x)| = 1. Apply normal_variation_algebra with S := S_x, ν₀ := ν(x), N := Dν(x), L := DZ(x), g := Dζ(x) and ζ := ζ(x) (its hypotheses are step 3 and step 1(b)): trace(P_x∘DZ(x)) = ζ(x)·trace(P_x∘Dν(x)) = 0 by the trace hypothesis (htr), and Σ_j(|DZ(x)u_j − P_xDZ(x)u_j|² − u_j·DZ(x)(P_xDZ(x)u_j)) = f₁(x) − ζ(x)²a(x) = q(x), where u_j = P_xe_j. Since ‖DZ(x)‖ ≤ Λ, jacobian_bound gives
 (4.1) √det(((I + tDZ(x))ι_x)*((I + tDZ(x))ι_x)) ≤ 1 + (t²/2)q(x) + C₀|t|³.

5. (The variation set.) K := tsupport Z is compact and K ⊆ U. E := M ∩ K is measurable (M measurable by (Meas), K closed) and H^m(E) < ∞ by (hfin). Put t₁ := min(t₀, 1, 1/(Λ + 1)) > 0; if |t| < t₁ then |t| ≤ 1, |t|Λ < 1 and |t| < t₀.

6. (Area comparison.) For |t| < t₁ let Φ_t(x) := x + tZ(x) and J(t,x) := √det((DΦ_t(x)ι_x)*(DΦ_t(x)ι_x)). Φ_t is C¹. By perturbation_injective (|t|Λ < 1), Φ_t is injective, DΦ_t(x) = I + tDZ(x), and DΦ_t(x) is injective for every x. The deformation hypothesis (hdef) and (hArea) applied to E and Φ_t give
 H^m(E) ≤ H^m(Φ_t(E)) ≤ ∫⁻_E ofReal(J(t,x)) dH^m.
 By (4.1) and DΦ_t(x) = I + tDZ(x), J(t,x) ≤ 1 + (t²/2)q(x) + C₀|t|³ for every x ∈ E.

7. (Measurability and bounds.) f₁, a and q are continuous on M (Dζ is continuous, x ↦ P_xe_j is continuous on M by step 3, Dν is continuous on O ⊇ M, ζ is continuous), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for H^m⌞M (M measurable) and therefore for H^m⌞E. Since ζ is C^∞ with compact support there are B₁, B₂ with |Dζ(x)| ≤ B₁ and |ζ(x)| ≤ B₂ for all x; since C' ⊆ O is compact there is B₃ with ‖Dν(x)‖ ≤ B₃ on C'. As |P_xe_j| ≤ |e_j| = 1: 0 ≤ f₁ ≤ P·B₁² everywhere, and for x ∈ M either x ∈ C' and 0 ≤ ζ(x)²a(x) ≤ B₂²·P·B₃², or x ∉ C' and ζ(x) = 0. Hence |q| ≤ B := PB₁² + B₂²PB₃² on M.

8. (Nonnegative second variation.) second_variation_nonneg with μ := H^m, E, J, q, B, C := C₀ and t₀ := t₁ (hypotheses: steps 5–7) gives ∫_E q dH^m ≥ 0.

9. (From E to M.) If x ∈ M ∖ E then x ∉ tsupport Z, so by step 1(c) ζ(x) = 0 and Dζ(x)(P_xe_j) = 0 (P_xe_j ∈ S_x); hence f₁(x) = 0 and q(x) = 0. Since M is measurable, ∫_M q = ∫_E q ≥ 0 (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero).

10. (Splitting.) f₁ and ζ²a are integrable on E (a.e.-measurable, bounded by step 7, H^m(E) < ∞) and vanish on M ∖ E (step 9), so they are integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero). Therefore 0 ≤ ∫_M q = ∫_M f₁ − ∫_M ζ²a, i.e. ∫_M (Σ_j|Dν(x)(P_xe_j)|²)·ζ(x)² dH^m = ∫_M ζ²a dH^m ≤ ∫_M f₁ dH^m, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: variation_field gives an admissible Z = ζν on M with DZ = (Dζ)ν + ζDν on span T_xM and ζ, Dζ vanishing on M off tsupport Z.

shape_operator + normal_variation_algebra: trace(P_x DZ(x)) = 0 and the second-order coefficient Q(S_x, DZ(x)) equals q(x) = |∇^Mζ|²(x) − ζ(x)²|A|²(x); jacobian_bound then gives J_t(x) ≤ 1 + (t²/2)q(x) + C₀|t|³.
perturbation_injective + deformation hypothesis + (hArea): H^m(M ∩ tsupport Z) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(J_t) for small |t|.
second_variation_nonneg gives ∫_{M∩tsupport Z} q ≥ 0; q = 0 on the rest of M, so ∫_M |A|²ζ² ≤ ∫_M |∇^Mζ|².
